To OP:

Write down the steps needed to do common tasks, such as how to put in the games properly (or find them on PC), how to load a save (may want to start with his commonly played games, and list the steps for each), and give him an overall talk about how to properly handle equipment (same as an adult would have with a small child).

Did he purchase the system for you (I don't know your age)? I ask, because you might be able to convince him to buy his own controller to use (or buy him one). That way, if he breaks the analog sticks, or rage-smashes it on the floor, it's not your controller being destroyed.

Best of luck!

I bought the PC and the PS3 on my own, albeit the PC monitor is his. We're not very rich and I can say for sure that buying gaming related stuff is the last on his list. I can't afford any replacements right now as I'm still paying off the new graphics card. My parents' mentality is that while I'm under their roof, what's mine is theirs and vice versa, see my problem? I can't move out because I don't have the means to do so.

I can talk to him about it, but he is a little senile or just doesn't care as much as I do about my stuff. It's not about the controller just. If you remember the old days of PS1 and PS2, if the disc doesn't read, he won't hesitate to hit the console a few times.

I definitely understand your situation. I'm just going over each possible solution, and I think that's still the best bet. Make the instructions easy to read and follow. Section it off, like a troubleshooting guide. Have a section for if the disc doesn't read, and so on.

People are stubborn. He may realize he is getting a bit senile; it likely frustrates him, and he probably doesn't want to admit it. Try and be patient with him if you do speak with him. Don't treat him like a child or condescendingly.

Instead, treat him like an adult and draw boundaries. Tell him you're worried about how he'll treat the property that you earned your own money to buy, and ask him to agree up front that if he breaks anything he'll replace it.

If you have this conversation there's a good chance you'll never need to talk about it again because he'll treat your things nicely to avoid the embarrassment of breaking another thing and replacing it...or he'll give zero fucks but won't be able to get mad when you demand replacements.
